question.problem: The variances of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ are $5$ and $20$, respectively. Given that $\text{Cov}(X,Y)=8,$ find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{5}, \\ \text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[Y]}=\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting our data in the formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[X]} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{5}\cdot 2\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
